extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent counsel seeking to accelerate international patent prosecution using the Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for determining PPH eligibility, preparing and filing PPH requests, and coordinating prosecution strategy across multiple patent offices to accelerate examination while managing risks to claim scope and patent strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive first office determination
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be at least one corresponding earlier application at a participating office where at least one claim has been found patentable/allowable (a completed examination or PCT search that yielded an allowable claim addressing novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OEE work product can be a notice of allowance, a positive office action, or a favorable PCT work product. The PPH request relies on that positive determination; without it you are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating office relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: The second application must be filed in an office that has a PPH agreement with the first office and the applications must have a recognized relationship (typically sharing the same earliest priority date or being the same PCT application entering different national phases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm bilateral/multilateral participation before filing; participation varies by office and over time. Provide documentary proof of priority linkage if the relationship is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the second application must 'sufficiently correspond' to the allowed claims from the first application—generally identical to or narrower in scope than the OEE's allowed claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You typically must amend OLE claims to match allowed OEE claims. New dependent claims that add limitations are usually acceptable (they’re narrower). Wholly new claims or omission of critical features break correspondence. Most offices require a claims correspondence table mapping each OLE claim to one or more allowed OEE claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPH request must be made before substantive examination begins in the Office of Later Examination (OLE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OLE examiner has already started examining the application (issued a first office action on the merits), it’s generally too late. Some non-substantive actions (e.g., a U.S. restriction requirement) don’t count as substantive exam. File the PPH request early—ideally right after filing or entry into national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal documentation required for a PPH request
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete PPH request normally includes a filled request form, copies of the OEE work product showing allowed claims, translations if required, copies of prior art cited by the OEE examiner, a claims correspondence table, and identification of any PCT work product for PCT‑PPH cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each office has specific forms (e.g., USPTO SB/20GLBL, EPO Form 1009). Ensure translations when documents are not in the OLE’s official language and provide prior art lists as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office‑specific procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual offices impose additional formalities or statutory steps that must be observed (e.g., the USPTO requires PCT national‑stage PPH requests to include an express request to start national‑phase examination early under 35 U.S.C. 371(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the latest office guidance/forms. The EPO integrates PPH into its PACE framework; some offices can pull documents via WIPO CASE/Global Dossier. A September 2023 USPTO review found many incorrect forms were used—procedural compliance is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility frameworks: Regular (Paris‑route) PPH vs PCT‑PPH
rubrics_metrics.description: Two main frameworks: Regular PPH relies on national/regional work products from regular patent applications; PCT‑PPH is based on favorable PCT work products such as WO/ISA, WO/IPEA, or an International Preliminary Examination Report (IPER).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each framework has distinct qualifying documents. For PCT‑PPH, the qualifying written opinion or IPER must indicate at least one claim meets novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common rejection reasons for PPH requests
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH requests are frequently refused for missing or incorrect translations, incomplete claim correspondence, examination already started, incorrect forms or formalities, and unclear priority linkage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PPH request is found defective, some offices allow correction—monitor the request status and correct deficiencies promptly. Ensure correct signing, up‑to‑date forms, and clear claim mapping to avoid denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: What PPH provides: accelerated examination and earlier decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When granted, the PPH request advances the application out of turn in the examination queue and aims to shorten time to first office action and final disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical timeframes cited: PPH at the USPTO averages ~7.5 months to first action vs 20–23 months for standard cases; IP5 average pendency ~4.8 months with PPH vs ~16 months without. Some smaller offices report even larger percentage reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: What PPH does not provide: no guarantee of allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH speeds examination but does not guarantee allowance or harmonize substantive law—each office applies its own laws and examination standards and conducts its own substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An allowed claim in one office may be rejected elsewhere due to different prior art or stricter criteria. Examiners may reuse prior work only to the extent it’s useful; do not assume automatic grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exemption from local rules or subject‑matter limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH does not change local procedural or substantive rules; local exclusions to patentable subject matter, rules on amendments, unity, or added matter still apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entering an office via PPH does not permit bypassing rules like EPO added‑matter restrictions or national exclusions (e.g., business‑method limitations). You remain bound by local law and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH is not a filing mechanism or alternative patent route
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH presupposes existing filings (Paris or PCT) in each country; it overlays on those filings and does not change filing routes, patent term, or create a separate patent type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must still file applications through normal channels; PPH only affects examination queue order, not filing substance or patent term adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic trade‑offs: potential to lock in narrowed claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Using PPH to present already‑narrowed claims across jurisdictions can foreclose the opportunity to obtain broader claims in other offices where different prior art or standards might have allowed broader protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether time savings are worth narrowing claim scope. Strategies include using PPH only in critical markets, pursuing broader claims in other jurisdictions through normal prosecution, or obtaining an early PPH allowance and keeping a continuation/divisional pending to pursue broader claims later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost efficiencies and statistical benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH often reduces prosecution duration and the number of office actions, lowering attorney, translation, and procedural costs; historical statistics show higher allowance rates for PPH cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: U.S. 2015 data showed 84% allowance for PPH vs 68% for regular applications; average office actions to allowance ~2.9 for PPH vs 3.1 for others. Taiwan reported 93% grant rate for PPH vs ~80% standard and fewer office actions. PPH typically has no government fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic coordination benefits (harmonization and enforcement planning)
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH enables applicants to harmonize claim scope across countries, simplifying licensing, fundraising due diligence, and multi‑jurisdiction enforcement planning when claims are consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinated claims make licensing and litigation strategy more straightforward. However, harmonization depends on substantive outcomes in each office—consistent grants strengthen validity arguments but do not guarantee litigation success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining PPH with other acceleration mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH can be compared or combined with alternatives (e.g., USPTO Track One, US age‑based acceleration, EPO PACE, UKIPO Green Channel) depending on costs, eligibility, and business needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PPH when you already have a positive foreign work product and want low‑cost acceleration. Use paid options (Track One) when you need prioritized U.S. examination regardless of foreign work product. Some offices limit overlapping special statuses—check office rules before combining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring status and correcting defective PPH requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should monitor PPH request status in office databases (e.g., Patent Center showing 'Advanced out of turn by PPH') and be prepared to correct procedural defects where permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct form use and watch for office status indicators. Some offices allow cure of defects; timely corrections avoid losing PPH benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible application types and explicit exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH generally does not apply to design patents, reissue applications, reexamination proceedings, or provisional patent applications; it applies to regular utility patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify eligibility for your specific application type before attempting PPH. Offices may have additional subject‑matter or pilot exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office participation, authoritative sources, and evolving coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in Global PPH changes over time; authoritative sources include the JPO’s PPH Portal (English), USPTO PPH page, and EPO PPH section, which list participating offices, start/end dates, and office requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm current participation (e.g., as of late 2023 ~55 offices, Brazil/ARIPO additions noted). Some significant offices (India) may not participate broadly—always check the up‑to‑date office portals.
